title: Dollar jumps after strong US payrolls report
description: The US dollar index jumped significantly following the Labor Department's report indicating an increase of 165,000 jobs last month, which far exceeded economists' forecasts. As a result, the probability of a rate hike from the Federal Reserve climbed to nearly 80% for next month. Moreover, Federal Reserve officials voiced concerns about ongoing inflation, leading to declines for other currencies such as the euro and sterling against the dollar.

title: Gold drops as strong US payrolls boost dollar, yields
description: In light of stronger-than-anticipated US payroll figures, gold prices dipped significantly as the data suggested a robust labor market. This development heightened expectations for sustained high-interest rates from the Federal Reserve, bolstering the dollar's strength. Spot gold saw a decline of 0.3% to reach $4,074.36 per ounce, while US gold futures fell by 0.9%. However, Indian retail demand picked up ahead of Diwali festivities, taking advantage of the lower prices.

title: Risk-off mood sweeps European stocks as AI concerns deepen
description: European markets saw a 1% dip as a wave of selloffs hit insurance stocks following a Democratic victory, raising concerns around the stability of AI investments. A significant downgrade of German reinsurers by JPMorgan added to the insurance sector's woes. Yet, clean energy stocks thrived, bolstered by renewed support for green initiatives.

title: Wall Street stocks rally after heavy AI-related selloff
description: Wall Street's trading session presented a mixed scenario as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq climbed, contrasting with a modest dip in the Dow. Investor apprehensions regarding impending regulations for the AI sector, especially after recent Democratic electoral successes, led to increased market volatility. Meanwhile, key global markets witnessed declines, particularly in Europe and Asia, overshadowing advancements in certain tech stocks amid a generally bearish sentiment.

title: Nasdaq rebounds but posts fourth straight weekly decline
description: On Friday, technology stocks saw a significant rebound, boosting investor optimism about growth in artificial intelligence amidst recent market fluctuations. The semiconductor sector soared, primarily driven by impressive gains from Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices. Although this recovery was strong, the Nasdaq recorded its fourth consecutive weekly fall, hinting at a mixed market outlook. Job indicators remain strong, influencing Federal Reserve interest rate hike expectations.

title: US stocks today: Nasdaq rebounds as chip stocks recover from steep losses, rate fears persist
description: US stocks rebound as chipmakers recover from Thursday's steep AI-led selloff, lifting the Nasdaq 1.73%. Nvidia, AMD, Intel and Micron lead the recovery, while stronger-than-expected October jobs data revive concerns over a December Fed rate hike. Airbnb rallies after raising its full-year revenue growth forecast, while Atlassian shares decline.

title: Stock Market Highlights: US stocks rebound, but Nasdaq posts fourth straight weekly decline
India's 10-year bond posts best week in 7 years, leads emerging Asia as oil slides
description: This week, Indian government bonds saw a remarkable performance, outpacing other Asian markets as benchmark yields dropped significantly. Following the Democratic win in the US midterms, crude prices fell sharply, enticing foreign investors back to purchase a significant volume of Indian bonds. This shift alleviates pressure on the Reserve Bank of India to maintain elevated yields, contributing to a positive outlook for Indian debt moving forward.

title: British Airways parent profit drops on higher fuel costs
description: IAG, the owner of British Airways and Iberia, said Friday that its net profit dropped more than 12 percent in the third quarter on soaring fuel costs and flight disruptions caused by the Middle East conflict. The group said its overall flight capacity had been hit "by cancellations due to the conflict in the Middle East, together with aircraft availability linked to engine issues and disruption related to air traffic control disruption".
